name: loom-l1

plan.approach: One new module (specpack.py) carries load/validate/alignment/slice/next/record as pure functions over the json; the CLI grows format detection (sdd.json ⇒ legacy, else <dirname>.json specpack) and a check command. The vendored schema + real python-jsonschema replace hand validation on this path. The wave dogfoods itself: the final task runs the new commands against this very file.

decisions.because: The in-session loop proves the protocol with the code we have; subprocess spawning adds surface without new understanding.

decisions.because: The repo standard is python-jsonschema with format checking; the legacy path is scheduled for retirement and not worth a rewrite this wave.

designs.detail: load_specpack(path), validate(doc) via python-jsonschema against the vendored schema; atomic save reusing spine.save; revision defaults to 1 when absent.
designs.title: Specpack loader + validator

designs.detail: alignment(doc) → sorted violation list for A1–A4 + coverage report (FR/AC/DES reached-by) for A5; evidence rule A6 checked at record time.
designs.title: Alignment checker

designs.detail: Format detection by file presence; check is specpack-only; next/record/status branch to the specpack functions; legacy path untouched.
designs.title: CLI integration: check/next/record/status over specpack

designs.detail: slice_for(doc, task_id): transitive closure over needs plus trace targets, canonical sorted render, sha256 digest of the canonical form.
designs.title: Slice compiler

diagrams.caption: L1 pipeline: specpack.json → loader (jsonschema) → alignment checker → next/record → specpack.json (atomic, revision-fenced)

clarifications.question: Does `loom run` (profile subprocess spawning, captured evidence) land in L1?

constraints.text: Determinism: same file + same command ⇒ byte-identical selections, ordering, and reports. Sorted ids everywhere; no map-iteration or clock-dependent rendering (clock lives only inside evidence rows the caller supplies).
The legacy sdd.json path stays read-only this wave — no regression on the 25 existing tests.
The specpack schema is vendored into the package; a test asserts the vendored copy's sha256 equals the docs copy (drift alarm, no docs-path coupling).

scenarios.then: exit 0 with FR-2 and DES-3 reported as gaps

scenarios.given: a specpack with a dangling needs id

requirements.text: `loom check <dir>` MUST load the initiative's specpack, validate it against the vendored schema, run alignment rules A1–A6, and print coverage in canonical (sorted) order. Exit 1 only on rule violations (A1–A4); coverage gaps are reported, never blocking.

scenarios.then: tasks arrive in id order among ready ones and DONE ends the loop
scenarios.when: loom next runs twice recording passes between

requirements.text: `loom next <dir>` MUST hand out exactly one actionable task — resumable doing, then ready todo (all needs done), id order — with its slice (flow + trace closure, sorted, digested); DONE or BLOCKED otherwise.

scenarios.when: record pass without a zero-exit command

requirements.text: `loom record <dir> --task T --result pass|fail|unblock|cancel` MUST append an evidence row, move states (pass⇒done on zero-exit evidence, fail⇒todo retry, two consecutive fails⇒blocked), refuse stale writers by revision, and refuse done without zero-exit evidence.

stories.so: the loop runs on the format I actually author
stories.want: loom to check, next, and record against a specpack file

spec.why: loom's prototype spine was hand-typed slop. The owner codified specpack 0.2; loom must manage context and loop through tasks directly on that format, with alignment verified every pass.
